title: Dimercaptosuccinic Acid (DMSA) Reduces Renal Uptake of 177Lu After [177Lu]Lu-Octreotate Administration in Mice
content: Radionuclide therapy with 177Lu-octreotate improves survival and quality of life in patients with metastatic neuroendocrine tumors, but outcomes are limited by radiation-induced renal and bone marrow toxicity. To reduce the absorbed dose to the kidneys, kidney blocking is routinely performed by co-injection of amino acids. However, more efficient kidney-blocking strategies may allow further optimization of 177Lu-octreotate treatment. The aim of this study was to evaluate DMSA as a kidney-blocking agent during 177Lu-octreotate treatment. DMSA and the amino acid L-lysine, alone or in combination, were given to female C57BL/6N mice at different doses and time points relative to administration of 5 MBq 177Lu-octreotate. All animals were euthanized 24 h after 177Lu-octreotate administration, and 177Lu activity concentrations in the kidneys, blood, and other organs were measured and compared to controls. Reduced 177Lu kidney uptakes were found across all DMSA dosages (adjusted p < 0.05), with generally larger reductions at higher DMSA doses. The largest kidney-protective effect was seen for 32 mg DMSA given simultaneously with 177Lu-octreotate, with a mean reduction in 177Lu kidney uptake of approximately 65%. DMSA combined with L-lysine showed no statistically significant additive kidney-protective effect. Overall, DMSA shows potential as a kidney-blocking agent for treatment with 177Lu-octreotate.
